title: Sifted colimits and separately colimit-preserving bifunctors
statement: Use universes, simplicial sets, quasicategories, spaces, coherent diagrams, products, weak contractibility and colimits as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the simplex category $\Delta$ as in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Write $\mathcal S$ for the infinity-category of small spaces. A small infinity-category $K$ is called sifted when its colimit functor $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)\to\mathcal S$ on small spaces preserves finite products, including the empty product. Every such $K$ is weakly contractible. If $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ are infinity-categories admitting $K$-indexed colimits and $F:\mathcal C\times\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ preserves them separately in each variable, then $F$ preserves $K$-indexed colimits as a functor on the product: for diagrams $P:K\to\mathcal C$ and $Q:K\to\mathcal D$, the canonical cocone to $F(\operatorname{colim}P,\operatorname{colim}Q)$ is colimiting. The nerve $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is sifted in this space-valued sense.
